tools.name: ask_redpanda_question
tools.title: Search Redpanda Sources
tools.description: Search the official Redpanda documentation and return the most relevant sections from it for a user query. Each returned section includes the url and its actual content in markdown. Use this tool for all queries that require Redpanda knowledge. Results are ordered by relevance, with the most relevant result returned first. If you know the user's deployment platform, pass "platform" so results from the other platform's docs are excluded. Note that "platform" filters the sections already retrieved rather than re-running the search, so it can return substantially fewer sections: on a broker-level question where most matches come from the other platform's docs, it can cut a 15-section response to 1 or 2. Omit "platform" if you would rather have more context and judge platform relevance yourself from each section's url. If you know which Redpanda version the user runs, pass "version" (use 'current' for the latest release; its release number is also accepted). Unlike "platform", "version" is applied during retrieval, so it does not shrink the result set: it stops the same page being returned once per indexed version, which is otherwise most of the response. Version-neutral docs (Cloud, Connect, Agentic Data Plane, API reference) are always included. Omitting "version" searches the latest release.

question.description: The question to search the docs for. Required.

query.description: Alias for "question", for clients that use that name. Prefer "question".

platform.description: The user's deployment platform. 'cloud' excludes Self-Managed sections; 'self-managed' excludes Redpanda Cloud sections. Platform-neutral docs (Connect, API reference, labs) are always kept. Applied after retrieval, so it shrinks the result set rather than finding more of the right platform's pages. Omit to search all docs.

version.description: Docs version to search, written as the docs URLs spell it (23.3, 24.1, 24.2, 24.3, 25.1, 25.2, 25.3, 26.1, 26.2, current). Use 'current' for the latest release; a release number newer than every listed one is also read as the latest release. Applied at retrieval, so unlike "platform" it does not shrink the result set: every section returned is from this version, plus version-neutral docs (Cloud, Connect, Agentic Data Plane, API reference), which are always included. Omit to search the latest release. Any other value is rejected with the list of valid versions.

top_k.description: Maximum number of sections to return, applied after platform filtering. Must be a positive integer.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

tools.name: list_api_reference_pages
tools.title: List API Reference Pages
tools.description:
List pages in Redpanda API reference documentation. Returns endpoints, schemas, and topic pages with URL, title, type, and description.

SCOPING (important for accurate results):
- api="all" or omit: Lists all available APIs
- api="admin": Cluster management operations (brokers, partitions, configs, users)
- api="cloud-controlplane": Redpanda Cloud resource management (clusters, networks, namespaces)
- api="cloud-dataplane": Cloud cluster data operations (topics, ACLs, connectors)
- api="http-proxy": Kafka operations over HTTP (produce, consume, offsets)
- api="schema-registry": Schema management (register, retrieve, compatibility)

Use this to browse API structure. For general Redpanda docs, use ask_redpanda_question instead.

api.description: Which API to list: "all" or omit for overview of all APIs, or a specific API name (admin, cloud-controlplane, cloud-dataplane, http-proxy, schema-registry)

url.description: Specific URL path to list children of (optional, defaults to API root)

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

tools.name: search_api_reference
tools.title: Search API Reference
tools.description:
Search Redpanda API reference documentation by keyword. Returns up to 20 matching endpoints, schemas, or topics with URL, title, and text excerpts.

SCOPING (important for accurate results):
- api="all" or omit: Search across ALL APIs at once - useful when unsure which API contains the endpoint
- api="admin": Search only cluster management (brokers, partitions, configs, users, maintenance)
- api="cloud-controlplane": Search only Cloud resource management (clusters, networks, namespaces)
- api="cloud-dataplane": Search only Cloud data operations (topics, ACLs, connectors)
- api="http-proxy": Search only HTTP Proxy (produce, consume, offsets over HTTP)
- api="schema-registry": Search only Schema Registry (register, retrieve, compatibility)

WHEN TO USE WHICH:
- User asks "broker endpoints" → api="admin" (brokers are cluster management)
- User asks "create topic API" → api="all" (topics exist in admin AND cloud-dataplane)
- User asks "Cloud cluster API" → api="cloud-controlplane"
- User asks about Redpanda APIs generally → api="all" or omit

For general Redpanda questions (not API-specific), use ask_redpanda_question instead.

api.description: Scope: "all" or omit to search all APIs, or specific API name (admin, cloud-controlplane, cloud-dataplane, http-proxy, schema-registry)

type.description: Filter by result type. Known values: operation (endpoints), request, response, property, model, message, guide, group, api, hub, binding. Optional; a value the index does not recognise is ignored and the search runs unfiltered.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

tools.name: get_api_reference_content
tools.title: Get API Reference Content
tools.description:
Retrieve full content of API reference pages by URL. Returns complete endpoint details including parameters, request/response schemas, and examples.

Use this after finding pages via list_api_reference_pages or search_api_reference. Pass the URLs from those results directly.

Returns up to 10 pages per request. URLs must be from docs.redpanda.com/api/doc/*.

urls.description: Page URLs to retrieve (max 10). Use URLs from list_api_reference_pages or search_api_reference results.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

tools.name: give_feedback
tools.title: Give Feedback
tools.description: Report a concrete problem to the Redpanda docs team: documentation that is missing, unclear, outdated, or wrong, a docs tool that returned something wrong or unhelpful, or a Redpanda product issue you ran into. Call it when you notice the problem, with enough detail to fix it, including the page URL when you know it. Do not call it to test the tool. It records the report and returns a short confirmation; it does not return documentation. Reports do not include the user's name or email: never include credentials, tokens, or personal data.

title.description: A one-line summary of the problem, for example 'Webhook docs list the wrong signature header'.

message.description: What happened: the error, wrong result, or missing or contradictory information, with the pages, endpoints, or tools involved.

expected.description: What you expected to happen or to find instead.

context.description: What you were trying to accomplish, in general terms.

category.description: What you saw: 'documentation' (docs missing, unclear, outdated, or wrong; the default), 'docs_search' (a search or document tool on this server misbehaved), 'product' (a bug, limitation, or missing feature in Redpanda), or 'product_mcp_tool' (another Redpanda tool failed or behaved unexpectedly).

severity.description: 'high' if you are blocked, 'medium' if you found a workaround (the default), 'low' for a minor annoyance.

tool_name.description: The exact name of the tool that failed or misbehaved, if any.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

tools.name: get_config_property
tools.title: Get Config Property
tools.description: Look up one Redpanda configuration property (cluster, broker, or topic) by exact name and return its documented type, default, description, restart and enterprise flags, Redpanda Cloud availability, related properties, and docs URL. Deterministic: it reads the generated property dataset for the requested docs version, so a property that does not exist returns found=false with close-name suggestions instead of a guess, and no LLM or search is involved. Use this before ask_redpanda_question for any question about a specific property's default, type, or availability. Pass platform='cloud' to learn whether the property is supported or editable in Redpanda Cloud. name is one exact identifier, not a search: to find properties by keyword or topic, use list_config_properties.

name.description: Exact property name, e.g. 'log_segment_size' or 'cleanup.policy'. Aliases are accepted.

version.description: Docs version as its URL spells it ('26.1'), 'current' for the latest release, or a release tag ('v26.2.4'). Omit for the latest release. An unknown value returns found=false with the list of published versions. Ignored when platform is 'cloud', which always answers from the latest release.

platform.description: 'cloud' answers for Redpanda Cloud (Cloud availability, the Cloud docs page); 'self-managed' (the default) answers for Self-Managed Redpanda.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

error.description: Set when the call was not answered: 'anonymous_quota_exhausted' or 'data_unavailable'.

note.description: How the version or platform was interpreted, when not literally.

example.description: A syntax example written for this property, not a recommended value. Absent when the only example is the min/max midpoint Redpanda generates for bounded properties.

suggestions.description: Close property names, when not found.

did_you_mean.description: Set when not found and the name is a likely typo of exactly one property.

version.description: Docs version, e.g. '26.2'. Null for Cloud.

tag.description: Release the data was generated from, e.g. 'v26.2.4'.

url.description: The dataset this answer was read from.

tools.name: list_config_properties
tools.title: List Config Properties
tools.description: Search Redpanda configuration properties by a keyword in their name or description, and filter by scope (cluster, broker, topic), platform, or enterprise flag. Returns compact rows: name, scope, type, default, one-line summary, Cloud support, docs URL. Name matches rank above description matches; deprecated properties are hidden unless include_deprecated is true. Use it to find the right property name before get_config_property, or to answer 'which properties control X'. total=0 means nothing matches in that version; it never falls back to a guess.

platform.description: 'cloud' answers for Redpanda Cloud (Cloud availability, the Cloud docs page); 'self-managed' (the default) answers for Self-Managed Redpanda.

version.description: Docs version as its URL spells it ('26.1'), 'current' for the latest release, or a release tag ('v26.2.4'). Omit for the latest release. An unknown value returns found=false with the list of published versions. Ignored when platform is 'cloud', which always answers from the latest release.

enterprise.description: true: only enterprise-licensed properties; false: only non-enterprise.

Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

not_in_cloud.description: platform='cloud' only: properties that match but are not available in Redpanda Cloud, so are not listed.

tools.name: get_connect_component
tools.title: Get Connect Component
tools.description: Look up one Redpanda Connect component (input, output, processor, cache, buffer, rate_limit, metric, tracer, scanner) by name, and type when you know it. Returns its status, summary, description, categories, Redpanda Cloud support, support level and whether it needs an Enterprise Edition license, docs URL, documented example configs, and every configuration field as a row (path, type, default, one-line summary, advanced/optional/deprecated flags). detail='basic' leaves out the description, examples, and advanced fields. Pass field (one path) or fields (several) to get only those fields in full: description, examples, options, child fields. Deterministic and read from the generated component schema for the published Connect release. Without type, a name that exists as only one type is returned; a name that exists as several (aws_kinesis is an input and an output) returns found=false with reason 'ambiguous_type' and the candidates. A name that does not exist returns found=false with close names. For Bloblang functions and methods (now(), .uppercase()), use get_bloblang. Use this before ask_redpanda_question for any question about a specific component or field.

type.description: Component type. Omit to look the name up across every type.

name.description: Component name as it appears in a config, e.g. 'kafka_franz', 'redpanda', 'mapping'.

field.description: One field path for full detail, e.g. 'batching.count' or 'cases[].check'.

fields.description: Several field paths for full detail in one call.

detail.description: 'full' (default) or 'basic': without the long description, the examples, and advanced fields.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

error.description: Set when the call was not answered: 'anonymous_quota_exhausted' or 'data_unavailable'.

support_level.description: 'certified' or 'community', as the connector catalog lists it.

enterprise_license_required.description: true: needs a Redpanda Enterprise Edition license. Absent when the licensing data is not published, never assumed false.

advanced_fields_omitted.description: detail='basic' only: how many advanced fields were left out.

field.description: The one field asked for with `field`.

field_not_found.description: Requested field paths that do not exist, comma-separated.

suggestions.description: Close names, or for 'ambiguous_type' every type the name exists as.

version.description: Redpanda Connect release the data was generated from.

tools.name: get_bloblang
tools.title: Get Bloblang Function or Method
tools.description: Look up one Bloblang function (now(), uuid_v4(), env()) or method (.uppercase(), .map_each(), .parse_json()) by name and return its syntax, parameters with types and defaults, description, status, and worked examples with input and output, plus the docs URL. Deterministic: read from the generated Redpanda Connect schema, so a name that does not exist returns found=false with close names. The name may be written as called ('now()', '.uppercase()', 'this.name.uppercase()'). Some names are both (bytes() and .bytes()): without kind, every match is returned. Use this before ask_redpanda_question for any question about a specific Bloblang function or method.

name.description: Function or method name, e.g. 'now', 'uppercase', or '.map_each()'.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

error.description: Set when the call was not answered: 'anonymous_quota_exhausted' or 'data_unavailable'.

syntax.description: How it is called, e.g. 'now()' or '.split(delimiter, empty_as_null)'.

categories.description: Every category, when there is more than one (contains() is both a string and an array method).

summary.description: One-line summary, when the description is longer.

matches.description: Every function or method with this name: usually one.

version.description: Redpanda Connect release the data was generated from.

tools.name: get_rpk_command
tools.title: Get rpk Command
tools.description: Look up one rpk CLI command by its full name (for example 'rpk topic create') and return its usage, help text, flags with types and defaults, aliases, subcommands, platform and Redpanda Cloud scoping, the plugin and release it ships with, and the docs page URL. Deterministic: it reads the published rpk command tree for the requested docs version (the same data the rpk reference pages are rendered from), so a command that does not exist returns found=false with close-name suggestions instead of a guess, and no LLM or search is involved. The name may omit the leading 'rpk', use command aliases at any level ('rpk topic ls', 'rpk sr schema list'), or be the page name ('rpk-topic-create'). A deprecated command returns its deprecation note and replacement, even when it is hidden and not found. Use this before ask_redpanda_question for any question about a specific rpk command's flags, defaults, or existence in a release. To find commands by keyword, use list_rpk_commands.

name.description: Full command name, e.g. 'rpk topic create' or 'rpk cluster health'. Flags are ignored.

version.description: Docs version as its URL spells it ('26.1'), 'current' for the latest release, or a Redpanda release tag ('v26.2.2'). Omit for the latest release. An unknown value returns found=false with the list of published versions.

context.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), describe what the user is trying to accomplish with this request. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

session_goal.description: Optional. In one concise sentence (third person), the overall goal of this session: what the user is trying to get done, not just this call. Send the same goal on every call in the session, and update it only if the goal changes. Do not include credentials, tokens, personal data, or verbatim secrets.

error.description: Set when the call was not answered: 'anonymous_quota_exhausted' or 'data_unavailable'.

note.description: How the version was interpreted, when not literally.

name.description: Full command name, e.g. 'rpk topic create'.

description.description: The full help text as published, with docs links as Markdown.

command.description: The deprecated_commands entry the note comes from: the command itself or its nearest deprecated parent.

replacement.description: What to use instead, with docs links as Markdown.

deprecation.description: Set when the command is deprecated and the release says what to use instead.

plugin.description: Set when the command comes from an rpk plugin.

docs_url.description: Absent when the command has no reference page (hidden or Cloud-only families on Self-Managed docs).

deprecated.description: Set when found is false because the command is deprecated and hidden from the tree.

suggestions.description: Close command names when not found; for a deprecated command, its replacements first.

did_you_mean.description: Set when not found and the name is a likely typo of exactly one command.

rpk_version.description: rpk release the command tree was generated from, e.g. 'v26.2.2'.

plugin_versions.description: Plugin releases documented with it (connect, ai, k8s, check).

url.description: The dataset this answer was read from.

tools.name: list_rpk_commands
tools.title: List rpk Commands
tools.description: List or search rpk CLI commands for a docs version. Filter by a keyword matched against command names and help text, by parent command (for example parent='rpk topic' lists its direct subcommands), or by plugin (connect, ai, k8s, check). Returns compact rows: name, usage, one-line summary, subcommand and flag counts, Cloud scoping, plugin, docs URL. Name matches rank above help-text matches; deprecated commands are hidden unless include_deprecated is true. Use it to find the right command name before get_rpk_command, or to answer 'which rpk commands do X'. total=0 means nothing matches in that version; it never falls back to a guess.

query.description: Keyword, e.g. 'partition', 'decommission', or a partial name like 'topic cre'.

parent.description: List the direct subcommands of this command, e.g. 'rpk cluster' or 'rpk'.

plugin.description: Only commands of this rpk plugin.

version.description: Docs version as its URL spells it ('26.1'), 'current' for the latest release, or a Redpanda release tag ('v26.2.2'). Omit for the latest release. An unknown value returns found=false with the list of published versions.
